## 5. Leave and Time   Off

The leave year runs from 01 January to 31 December. All leave is applied for in Workbench and requires manager approval before it is taken, except emergency sick leave, which may be regularised within two working days.

Table 5.1 - Leave entitlements for FT-R employees, India entity. Pro-rated for FTC, PT and mid-year joiners.

| Maternity           | 26 weeks              | Statutory     | N/A             | No           |
| Paternity / partner | 4 weeks               | Per event     | N/A             | No           |
| Bereavement         | 5 days                | Per event     | N/A             | No           |
| Sabbatical          | Up to 12 weeks        | After 5 years | N/A             | Unpaid       |
| Public holidays     | 10 fixed + 2 floating | Calendar      | No              | No           |', '[source: employee_handbook.pdf, relevance: 0.43]
## 5.2 Approval   thresholds

- 1-3 days: reporting manager.
- 4-10 days: reporting manager and skip-level manager.
- 11+ days or any leave during a code freeze: function head, with a documented cover plan.
- Negative leave balance: People Operations only, capped at 5 days.', '[source: employee_handbook.pdf, relevance: -2.63]
## 3.3 Overtime and on-call

Non-exempt employees who work beyond 45 hours in a week accrue compensatory time at 1.25× or, where local law requires, overtime pay. On-call rotations are capped at one week in four; on-call allowance is ₹1,200 per weekday night and ₹2,500 per weekend day. A person who is paged between 00:00 and 06:00 may start the following workday no earlier than 13:00 without using leave.']
response: Full-time employees get 12 days of sick leave.

user_input: If I'm a probationary full-time employee, what benefits do I get and how long is my notice period?
retrieved_contexts:
['[source: employee_handbook.pdf, relevance: 1.71]
## 2. Employment   Basics and Classification

Every engagement at Northwind falls into one of five classifications. Classification determines eligibility for leave, benefits, notice periods and equity participation.

| Class   | Description                        | Probation   | Notice   | Benefits     |
|', '|', '|', '-|', '-|', '--|
| FT-R    | Full-time regular                  | 90 days     | 60 days  | Full         |
| FT-P    | Full-time probationary             | 90 days     | 15 days  | Medical only |
| FTC     | Fixed-term contract ( ≤ 24 months) | 30 days     | 30 days  | Pro-rated    |

Table 2.1 - Employment   classifications and associated entitlements.

| Class   | Description                | Probation   | Notice   | Benefits     |
|', '|', '-|', '-|', '-|', '--|
| PT      | Part-time ( ≤ 24 hrs/week) | 60 days     | 30 days  | Pro-rated    |
| INT     | Intern / apprentice        | None        | 7 days   | Stipend only |', '[source: employee_handbook.pdf, relevance: -1.01]
## 2.2 Confirmation   of   employment

Probationary employees are reviewed at day 45 (informal) and day 85 (formal). A confirmation decision must be recorded in Workbench before day 90; absent a recorded decision, the employee is automatically confirmed. Probation may be extended once, by a maximum of 60 days, with written justification approved by the function head.', "[source: employee_handbook.pdf, relevance: -1.32]
## 10.3 Resignation and   notice

Resignations are submitted in Workbench and acknowledged within two working days. Notice periods are per Table 2.1. Notice buyout is permitted at the function head's discretion at the rate of one day of gross salary per day waived. Full and final settlement is released within 45 days of the last working day."]
response: For probationary full-time employees (FT-P), benefits are full. The notice period is 15 days. This information is detailed in Table 2.1 of the employee handbook, which specifies a probationary period of 90 days with full benefits and a 15-day notice period.
